UK basis: Rotterdam duty-paid premiums include EU import duty and EU CBAM (charging since 1 Jan 2026), which a UK importer does not pay; UK tariff, UK CBAM (not before 2027) and Rotterdam→UK freight were not researched.

Current-book findings (confident): (1) C110 ETP copper SHEET £10.77 and C101 ETP copper BAR £11.05 are below LME copper alone (£10.9977/kg, 8 Oct) and cathode+Aurubis premium (£11.2355/kg) — a semi-finished product cannot cost less than its cathode; both are low by at least the (unfound) conversion premium. (2) CZ121/CW614N rod £7.70 and CW617N forging brass £7.90 vs a European mill's published rod price £8.4753/kg (Almag, 9 Oct 2026, €9,990/t) — ~£0.6–0.8/kg (8–10%) low; £7.70 is ≈ bare Cu/Zn content (£7.4918). (3) PB1 phosphor-bronze BAR £13.91 is below its virgin Cu+Sn content £14.1115/kg (Sn from 12 Aug).

Current-book findings (likely, evidence dated/indirect): A380 £2.80 / ADC12 £2.75 / AlSi10Mg £2.89 / A365 £2.77 sit ~£0.65–0.80/kg above the only 2026 European DIN226 ingot print (£2.104/kg, Jan 2026) and above LME cash (£2.3658) — consistent with RULES' note that casting £/kg was a delivered-foundry figure; secondary ingot trades at or below LME. AZ91D £3.81 / AM60B £3.66 vs Chinese Mg ingot FOB £1.6985/kg and AZ91D ex-works £1.6537 — a gap of ~£2/kg that freight/duty alone is unlikely to explain, but no European Mg price was found to prove it.
Consistent with evidence: extrusion billet rows (6063 £3.27 vs LME + Aug DDP N. Germany billet premium £3.1981), LG2 £11.44 vs metal content £11.5976, CZ108 sheet £8.42 vs content £7.9846.
